title: Early Writing
introduction: Learn about early writing through simple examples and practice.
definition: Writing letters and short words helps us share ideas. Practise drawing lines, tracing letters and copying words.
rules: Practise holding a pencil comfortably, forming letters and writing from left to right.
Start with lines and curves, then letters, words and short phrases.
Copy words with different shapes: bag, cup, hen, fish, kite, leaf, moon, ring, tree, van.
Leave a small space between words.
Use a pencil and paper to trace letters.

examples.question: Copy a word with three letters.
steps: Write b, a and g in order.

examples.question: Copy a word with a tall letter.
steps: Form l clearly, then e, a and f.

examples.question: Copy two words with a space.
steps: Leave a space between red and hat.

examples.question: Copy a short statement.
steps: Use a capital I and a full stop.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: cup
exercises.solution: Copy the letters c, u, p from left to right.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: hen
exercises.solution: Copy the letters h, e, n from left to right.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: fish
exercises.solution: Copy f, i, s, h in order.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: kite
exercises.solution: Copy k, i, t, e in order.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: leaf
exercises.solution: Copy l, e, a, f in order.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: moon
exercises.solution: Copy m, o, o, n; remember both o letters.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: red hat
exercises.solution: Leave one space between red and hat.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: big dog
exercises.solution: Leave one space between big and dog.

exercises.question: Copy exactly: I can run.
exercises.solution: Start with capital I, leave spaces between words and finish with a full stop.

summary: Writing letters and short words helps us share ideas. Practise drawing lines, tracing letters and copying words.
